customer-order.gym.yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schemas/gym-exercise.schema.json
id: "customer-order"
title: "One customer per order"
transition:
  from: "novice"
  to: "initiate"
exitPerformance: >-
  Model a binary fact type from clean prose, give both object types
  reference schemes, and place the single-role uniqueness constraint
  that makes the business rule hold.
brief: |
  A customer places orders, and each order is placed by exactly one
  customer. Model the object types Customer and Order, add a fact type
  that relates them, and constrain it so that a single order can never be
  recorded as placed by two different customers.
reading: >-
  Skim (optional): Halpin & Morgan 3rd ed. -- ch. 3 (elementary facts),
  ch. 4 (uniqueness constraints). Deep reading is not expected before
  attempting.
reference: "customer-order.reference.orm.yaml"
checks:
  - kind: "requires_element"
    element:
      entity: "Order"
    diagnosis: >-
      Attribute-first thinking keeps Order as a field on Customer; in ORM
      every thing you state facts about is an object type of its own.
    reading: "Halpin & Morgan 3rd ed. -- ch. 3, sections 3.2-3.4 (elementary facts and object types)."
  - kind: "requires_element"
    element:
      factTypeBetween: ["Customer", "Order"]
    diagnosis: >-
      The relationship itself is a fact type -- "Customer places Order" --
      not a foreign key or an attribute; without it the model states no
      fact connecting the two.
    reading: "Halpin & Morgan 3rd ed. -- ch. 3, section 3.4 (fact types and readings)."
  - kind: "must_validate"
    diagnosis: >-
      A structurally invalid model usually means a missing reference
      scheme: every entity type needs a way to be identified before any
      fact about it is well-formed.
    reading: "Halpin & Morgan 3rd ed. -- ch. 5, section 5.3 (reference schemes)."
  - kind: "forbids_population"
    factType: "Customer places Order"
    constraint: "internal_uniqueness"
    hint: "Put a single-role uniqueness constraint on the Order role -- each order is placed by at most one customer."
    diagnosis: >-
      Treating constraints as decoration leaves the fact type unconstrained,
      so the model happily records the same order placed by two customers.
      The uniqueness constraint is the business rule, not an afterthought.
    reading: "Halpin & Morgan 3rd ed. -- ch. 4, sections 4.1-4.3 (internal uniqueness constraints)."
customer-order.reference.orm.yaml:
orm_version: "4.0"
model:
  name: Customer places Order
  object_types:
    - id: Customer
      name: Customer
      kind: entity
      reference_mode: customer_id
      definition: A party that places orders.
    - id: Order
      name: Order
      kind: entity
      reference_mode: order_id
      definition: A request a customer places.
  fact_types:
    - id: Customer_places_Order
      name: Customer places Order
      roles:
        - id: Customer_places_Order.places
          player: Customer
          role_name: places
        - id: Customer_places_Order.is_placed_by
          player: Order
          role_name: is placed by
      readings:
        - "{0} places {1}"
        - "{1} is placed by {0}"
      constraints:
        - type: internal_uniqueness
          roles:
            - Customer_places_Order.is_placed_by
          id: Each_Order_is_placed_by_at_most_one_Customer
          minted_from: '{"type":"internal_uniqueness","roles":[[1,"is placed by",{"name":"Customer places Order","readings":["{0} places {1}","{1} is placed by {0}"],"players":["Customer","Order"]}]],"fact_type":{"name":"Customer places Order","readings":["{0} places {1}","{1} is placed by {0}"],"players":["Customer","Order"]}}'
        - type: mandatory
          role: Customer_places_Order.is_placed_by
          id: Each_Order_is_placed_by_at_least_one_Customer
          minted_from: '{"type":"mandatory","role":[1,"is placed by",{"name":"Customer places Order","readings":["{0} places {1}","{1} is placed by {0}"],"players":["Customer","Order"]}],"fact_type":{"name":"Customer places Order","readings":["{0} places {1}","{1} is placed by {0}"],"players":["Customer","Order"]}}'
